description: QRShield Evaluator Sample Lab Specimens - Reproducible, deterministic benchmark test cases

samples.name: Official Registered Merchant QR
samples.summary: Authentic merchant payment QR code matching both registered trusted destination and visual reference baseline.
samples.description: Demonstrates successful verification of a genuine merchant QR code. The payment address matches the active database registry record, camera image quality meets all thresholds, and physical appearance matches the merchant's registered reference baseline.
samples.creation_method: Deterministic QR generation via qrcode (v4 error correction level M, 400x400 px, margin 4). Rendered with high contrast and optimal sharpness.

samples.name: Replaced QR Code (Destination Mismatch)
samples.summary: Malicious QR code redirecting funds to an unauthorized attacker account instead of the merchant's registered account.
samples.description: Demonstrates detection of a payment destination override attack. An attacker has generated a fraudulent QR code bearing the store's name but redirecting payments to an unauthorized attacker VPA. The system detects the destination conflict against the trusted registry.
samples.creation_method: Deterministic QR generation using attacker payment payload (pa=attacker-sample@upi) evaluated against the merchant's registered registry destination (pa=qrshield-sample@icici).

samples.name: Unregistered Merchant Destination
samples.summary: QR code containing a readable payment address that has no active trust anchor in the verified registry.
samples.description: Demonstrates handling of an unanchored payment destination. The QR is technically decodable, but the payment address has never been registered by a verified merchant. The system surfaces an informational warning without falsely accusing the merchant of fraud.
samples.creation_method: Deterministic QR generation with an unregistered payment address (pa=unregistered-sample@upi) evaluated with no merchant context or registry match.

samples.name: Physical Sticker / Border Tampering
samples.summary: QR code with valid destination but showing clear visual perimeter cutlines / sticker overlay anomalies against the baseline.
samples.description: Demonstrates detection of physical QR tampering (e.g. pasted sticker overlay). The scanned payload matches the merchant's destination, but deterministic homographic and perimeter edge analysis reveals an anomalous rectangular boundary cutline.
samples.creation_method: Deterministic QR baseline composited with an edge cutline perimeter overlay (340x340 px rectangular stroke in quiet zone) that triggers boundaryAnomalyDetected in the tamper analysis engine while preserving decodability.

samples.name: Degraded Camera Capture (Insufficient Evidence)
samples.summary: Severely underexposed, blurred, and low-contrast capture where image quality is insufficient for authoritative verification.
samples.description: Demonstrates safe handling of degraded photography. Although the matrix is barely decodable through Reed-Solomon parity recovery, the image quality analyzer flags multiple severe defects (low resolution, extreme underexposure, blur, low contrast). Rather than risking a false negative, the system requires a clearer capture.
samples.creation_method: Baseline QR downsampled to 140x140 px, underexposed to 0.18 mean brightness, and blurred via Gaussian filter (sigma 0.8), triggering imageQuality.overallQuality = INSUFFICIENT.
